claims.text: The starting HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa.
The starting HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a quasi-static compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The starting HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a quasi-static fracture strain of 13.5%.
Approximately 3 at% Nb will partially replace Ta in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Replacing part of the Ta with Nb will alter the alloy's phase stability and phase-transformation kinetics during rapid loading.
The Nb-modified alloy will form fine Nb-rich precipitates dynamically during high-strain-rate deformation.
The Nb modification will activate metastable phase transformations and transformation-induced plasticity during dynamic loading.
Nb-rich precipitates or transformation products will distribute deformation more uniformly.
Nb-induced precipitation and phase transformation will increase strain hardening.
Nb-induced precipitation and phase transformation will inhibit localized shear banding and delay rapid failure.
The Nb-modified alloy will exhibit a 10–20% increase in yield strength relative to the baseline.
The Nb-modified alloy will increase strain to localization by approximately 5–10% relative to the baseline.
The Nb-modified alloy will have greater resistance to shear localization than the baseline alloy.
The Nb-modified alloy will exhibit reduced impact-induced energy release, indicating improved resistance to rapid failure.
The predicted improvements apply under adiabatic impact loading at strain rates around 10^3 s^-1.
The predicted improvements may not extend to lower strain rates or thermally managed loading conditions.

contradictions.description: The numerical baseline is explicitly quasi-static, while the predicted improvements and matched experiment concern dynamic loading near 10^3 s^-1. It is therefore unclear whether the claimed 10–20% strength and 5–10% localization-strain improvements are relative to the reported quasi-static values or to dynamically tested baseline specimens.
